title: The Third Path
next_chapter_hook: The silence of the Destiny Scribe was torn apart by a golden light, and it finally uttered the secret buried for countless eons—the Third Path requires first completing Chen Tianming's final task.

text.content:
Blood.

It was her blood.

Chen Ji knelt amidst the shattered Star Map formation lines, his knees sinking into the scorched earth, his ten fingers digging deep into the mud. That crimson figure lay less than three feet before him—Su Qingyao's robes soaked through with blood, the sword wound across her chest nearly piercing through her body still gushing blood.

Her lips were moving.

Chen Ji heard no sound. His ears were filled only with a sharp buzzing, as if someone were striking an eternal funeral bell inside his skull. He could only see her lips parting and closing, see in her eyes that gentle smile he had never witnessed before.

This woman, even unto death, was smiling.

dialogue.content:
'Don't... die...'

Chen Ji lunged forward, pulling Su Qingyao's cooling body tightly into his embrace. She was still breathing, thin as a silk thread, but she was. Blood seeped through his fingers, the warm sensation like a searing brand, burning through the shell of indifference he had cultivated for decades.

text.content:
Heart pierced like by a blade.

This is what 'heart pierced like by a blade' truly means.

Chen Ji had never imagined these four characters would manifest so concretely before him. His chest was truly aching, so intensely he could barely breathe, as if someone had seized his heart directly and was slowly tightening their grip.

He had orchestrated schemes across the world, leaving nothing to chance, treating everyone as a chess piece—yet he had failed to account for one person taking a sword for him.

'Why...' His voice was hoarse beyond recognition. 'Who told you to come!'

Su Qingyao's eyelids trembled, as if trying to open, but ultimately lacked the strength.

dialogue.content:
'Because she knew.'

That voice rang out again, cold, hollow, devoid of any trace of emotion. The Destiny Scribe's projection materialized from the void's rift, golden and black runes swirling around it like a prison, or like a throne.

'She knew from the very beginning that you were notrash. She investigated you, tracked you, but after the seventy-third verification, she chose to abandon the investigation and become your guardian.'

Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his grief instantly replaced by boundless fury: 'It was you! You deliberately made her stand in the way of that sword!'

text.content:
The Destiny Scribe's projection remained motionless, and on that faceless face, a hint of indecipherable meaning seemed to appear.

'No.' Its voice was calm to the point of cruelty. 'That sword was meant for you. She forcibly altered the thread of causality, stripping death from you and grafting it onto herself. This was the destined fate you deserved as master of the Tianji Record—yet she devoured this fate using the power of 'Shared Destiny'.'

Chen Ji trembled violently.

Shared Destiny.

That was Su Qingyao's exclusive ability unlocked at max affection, capable of sharing his Heavenly Fate consumption. But he had never imagined this bond would manifest in such a brutal manner.

dialogue.content:
'I ask you of two paths.' Chen Ji's voice suddenly became eerily calm, the calmness that only appeared when his rage reached its peak. 'The first path—grant me instantly overwhelming power to crush all. The second path—let me return to where everything began, to start anew.'

He rose slowly, carefully placing Su Qingyao's body on the ground, covering her meticulously with his outer robe.

'Tell me, what are the costs of these two paths?'

The Destiny Scribe fell silent for three breaths. During those three moments, Chen Ji sensed an immense pressure gathering, as if the entire heavens and earth were holding their breath, awaiting an answer.

'The first path,' the Destiny Scribe finally spoke, 'costs the complete zeroing of your remaining Heavenly Fate Value, plus eternal pursuit by the Heavenly Eye. You will become the enemy of all three realms while at your power's apex, never to die, never to cease fighting.'

'The second path costs you erasing every trace of your existence. Your friends, enemies, beloved, rivals—all will have their memories of you erased. You will start anew in a fresh life, but no one will remember you ever existed.'

Chen Ji closed his eyes. Two paths—one would make him an enemy of all beneath heaven, the other would erase him from the world. Either way, a complete tragedy.

'So this is the choice you give me?' Chen Ji abruptly opened his eyes, light exploding from his gaze. 'Make me choose between being the enemy of all under heaven, and being a person who doesn't exist?'

He laughed coldly, that smile full of mockery and defiance.

'Destiny, what kind of person do you think Chen Ji is? A chess piece you manipulate? The inheritor of the Tianji Record? I'll tell you—'

He stepped forward, his aura surging violently.

'I refuse to walk the path you give me!'

text.content:
The moment his words fell, the remaining Heavenly Fate Value within Chen Ji began to fluctuate violently. He felt the Tianji Record Fragment in his Mental Sea shaking frantically, as if responding to his unwilling heart.

The Destiny Scribe did not speak.

On that faceless face, the speed of rune circulation suddenly slowed by three degrees, as if some emotion was brewing within.

One breath.

Two breaths.

Three breaths.

'...You truly are different from the others.' For the first time, a certain fluctuation appeared in the Destiny Scribe's voice. 'Chen Tianming, when leaving the Tianji Record, said—'If a future inheritor can question the injustice of destiny, only then are they qualified to know the third matter.'

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

'The Third Path?'

The Destiny Scribe's projection drifted slowly toward him, each step increasing the pressure. Countless golden runes exploded in the void, weaving into a grand and ancient scroll—on that scroll, Chen Ji saw scenes from countless past eons, saw the final fates of each Tianji Record inheritor.

Without exception, all had died.

'The first and second paths are the destiny of all past inheritors.' The Destiny Scribe's voice echoed in the empty space. 'But before his death, Chen Tianming exhausted his final trace of Heavenly Fate, opening an untraveled path for those who came after.'

It paused.

'The Third Path—the Path of Fusion.'

text.content:
'The Path of Fusion...' Chen Ji murmured.

'As the name suggests,' the Destiny Scribe continued, 'you must simultaneously defeat two ultimate existences—one is your future self who inherited part of the Tianji Record's authority; the other is the Will's本体 that has dwelt above the heavenly dao since ancient times.'

Chen Ji's breathing suddenly grew heavy.

His future self. This meant he would fight against himself, against another 'Chen Ji' who had walked the paths he had not and possessed powers he did not.

And the Heavenly Eye—that terrifying existence that had followed him since Scroll Eight, the mastermind that treated all prophets as chess pieces.

choice.prompt:
Chen Ji clenched his fists tight, his knuckles white from the force. He stared directly at the Destiny Scribe, his voice low but firm.

'What is the cost of the Third Path? Don't tell me there is no cost—I don't believe there is any good thing in this world that can be gained without sacrifice.'

choices.description: Directly ask about the cost of the Third Path, accepting no concealment.
choices.visible_reward: Learn the Complete Truth of the Third Path
choices.risk_hint: The truth may be crueler than imagined

text.content:
The Destiny Scribe fell silent.

On that faceless projection, the speed of rune circulation slowed to an extreme, as if even it hesitated over how to speak.

After a long while, its voice rang out again, this time lacking the earlier coldness, carrying instead an indescribable...solemnity.

choices.description: Test the Destiny Scribe with a mocking attitude, maintaining psychological offensive.
choices.visible_cost: May provoke the Destiny Scribe's anger
choices.visible_reward: Gain the upper hand in momentum, control the initiative of the dialogue

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji let out a derisive laugh that echoed through the empty Void, carrying an indescribable mockery.

"The path of fusion? That does sound more noble than the previous two paths." He stood with hands clasped behind his back, cold light flickering in his eyes. "I'm just curious—if this path is so perfect, why has no one ever walked it?"

He stepped forward, glaring at the Fate Scribe.

"Is it because it's impassable, or because the cost is so great that even you dare not reveal it easily?"

choices.description: A strategy of stillness to overcome movement, waiting for the other party to proactively reveal more information.
choices.visible_cost: Silence might be perceived as weakness
choices.visible_reward: Let the Fate Scribe proactively reveal more hidden information
choices.risk_hint: The other party might use silence to apply pressure

text.content:
Chen Ji did not speak.

He simply stared quietly at the Fate Scribe, his gaze as calm as still water. Decades of scheming had taught him one thing—sometimes, silence is more deadly than any words.

As expected, the Fate Scribe broke the silence first.

"You're not going to ask?" Its tone carried a hint of surprise. "This is not the Chen Ji I know."

dialogue.content:
The Fate Scribe fell silent for a long time.

So long that Chen Ji almost thought it would never speak again.

Then, the countless runes suddenly dimmed, and on that faceless face, a twisted smile emerged—it was the first time Chen Ji saw something like an "expression" on this projection.

"The cost?" Its voice became ethereal. "The cost of the third path is ten thousand times more残忍 than the previous two."

It slowly raised a hand composed of runes, pointing at Chen Ji's chest.

"You need to completely dissipate in this battle—not death, but a total erasure of your soul, karma, and threads of fate. You will no longer exist in any corner of past, present, or future. Within the three realms, nothing will remember that you ever came."

text.content:
Chen Ji froze.

Complete dissipation.

Not even a soul remaining.

Not being forgotten by the world like the second path, but being fundamentally and utterly erased. He would lose the qualification for reincarnation, the possibility of rebirth at the other shore, everything—even the fact of having "once existed."

"However," the Fate Scribe's voice continued, "in exchange, everything you leave behind will eternally exist in another form. Your will shall become the new Heavenly Secrets that sustains the three realms, replacing the Heavenly Fate as the core of three-realm order. Your existence will not be remembered, but your order will endure forever."

dialogue.content:
"In other words—" the Fate Scribe's voice suddenly rose, runes exploding into scattered starfire across the Void. "You will trade self-dissolution for eternal order. The moment you dissipate, the Heavenly Fate will completely fall, and the three realms will usher in true peace. And you will become that eternal, formless guardian."

Chen Ji stood motionless.

Countless images flooded his mind—his years of scheming across the world, his tangled relationship with Su Qingyao, his promise to his sister Chen Nian, his pursuit of the truth behind the Tianji Record...

If he chose the third path, all of this would become meaningless.

Because he would cease to exist.

text.content:
"What? Scared?" The Fate Scribe's tone carried a hint of mockery. "I thought you would be different from others. It seems, no matter who it is, everyone retreats when facing true death."

Chen Ji lifted his head abruptly.

On that face that had remained calm for decades, a complex emotion rarely appeared—not fear, not anger, but an indescribable struggle and reluctance.

"I didn't say I would retreat." His voice was hoarse. "I was just thinking..."

He lowered his gaze, falling on the blood-soaked crimson figure collapsed behind him.

"If I choose this path, what will happen to her?"

dialogue.content:
The Fate Scribe paused for a moment.

"Her?"

"Su Qingyao." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet carried unwavering resolve. "She used 'shared fate' to block that sword for me. If I dissipate, what will happen to her?"

This time, the Fate Scribe was silent even longer.

"The essence of 'shared fate' is karmic binding." It finally spoke. "If you completely dissipate, the bound karmic thread will also break. She... will lose all memories related to you, as if you two never met."

Chen Ji closed his eyes.

That meant Su Qingyao would forget him. Forget everything she did for him, forget her years of protection and entanglement, forget her resolute determination to trade her life for his.

She would live, but not remember he ever existed.

choice.prompt:
Chen Ji stood there quietly, bearing this cruel truth. His heart was engaged in a fierce struggle—on one side, eternal peace for the three realms; on the other, the memories and existence of the person he cared about.

The Fate Scribe quietly awaited its verdict.

choices.description: Choose self-dissolution for eternal peace of the three realms, letting Su Qingyao forget you.
choices.visible_cost: Complete dissipation, losing all memories and existence
choices.visible_reward: Eternal peace for the three realms, Su Qingyao can survive
choices.risk_hint: This will be an irreversible and utter annihilation

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath.

He slowly turned, taking a last look at Su Qingyao. That pale face still faintly showed her usual stubbornness and pride; the wound on her chest was slowly healing, but no one knew when she would wake.

"I agree."

Three words, light as a feather, yet heavy as a thousand catties.

"But before that—" his gaze suddenly sharpened. "I must first accomplish one thing."

choices.description: Unable to accept Su Qingyao forgetting him, choose to abandon this path.
choices.visible_cost: Give up the possibility of eternal peace for the three realms
choices.visible_reward: Retain all bonds and memories with Su Qingyao
choices.risk_hint: Will face even more difficult choices

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji shook his head.

The movement was slight, yet carried unwavering resolve.

"No."

Only one word, but it made the runes around the Fate Scribe violently tremor.

"I have schemed across the world for decades, calculating all the heroes under heaven, never for the sake of any three-realm peace." Chen Ji's voice was low and calm. "I only wanted the people I care about to live well. If this path requires her memories as the cost—"

He lifted his head, eyes blazing with fierce light.

"Then I would rather not have this path."

choices.description: Before making a decision, first clarify the specific conditions and limitations of the third path.
choices.visible_reward: Gain the information needed to make the best choice
choices.risk_hint: The more information, the harder the choice

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji narrowed his eyes.

"You say Chen Tianming left this path," he said slowly, "then why didn't he take it himself? Why did he leave all this to me?"

The Fate Writer fell silent.

That silence itself was an answer.

"He couldn't take it." Chen Ji arrived at the answer himself. "Because he couldn't find a replacement. So he had to wait—wait for someone stronger than him, someone who could bear this burden better."

A cold smile crossed his face.

"And I'm that person?"

Chen Ji's question echoed through the void, and the Fate Writer's projection trembled violently.

Those golden runes began rearranging in an eerie manner, as if forced by Chen Ji's relentless questioning to reveal a sliver of truth.

"... Yes." The Fate Writer's voice was low and weary. "Before his death, Chen Tianming poured his final thread of Heavenly Fate into the seams of the timeline, waiting for someone capable of bearing this immense burden."

It paused.

"Across countless epochs, he screened countless inheritors. Only you—Chen Ji—passed all the trials."

Chen Ji's heart tightened: "What trials?"

text.content:
"The first trial—you were able to endure for decades under the guise of atrash without exposure, proving you possess absolute self-control and patience."

"The second trial—you were able to bring the three major sects, the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, and even the Eye of Heaven into your chess game, proving you possess the ability and ambition to scheme for the world."

"The third trial—" The Fate Writer's voice suddenly turned strange. "When you possessed absolute power, you still chose to protect those around you. This is the most difficult trial, because it means you won't abandon your humanity for power."

Chen Ji fell silent.

He had never imagined that those choices he considered merely不得已 would all be part of some trial.

dialogue.content:
"But there is one final trial," the Fate Writer's voice became profound. "It is sealed within Chen Tianming's final mission. Only by completing that mission can you qualify to walk the third path."

Chen Ji raised his head abruptly: "What mission?"

The Fate Writer did not answer directly.

It merely slowly unfolded that palm made of runes, projecting a blurry image into the void—in that image, a vague silhouette stood before an ancient stone gate, and carved above that gate were four characters:

Heavenly Fate's End.

"When you find that gate," the Fate Writer's voice drifted distant and ethereal, "you will know the answer."

text.content:
Before the words even finished, the Fate Writer's projection began to dissipate.

Countless golden runes scattered like fireflies, casting flickering light across this space. Chen Ji stood in place, watching that mysterious projection gradually fade, his mind swirling with countless thoughts.

The third path.

The path of fusion.

The price: self-annihilation, in exchange for eternal peace across the three realms.

He lowered his head, gazing at his bloodstained hands.

After scheming for the world all these years, he had always treated others as chess pieces. But now, he finally realized—from the very beginning, he himself had been merely a piece on someone else's chessboard.

But so what?

The corner of Chen Ji's lips slightly lifted, forming a profound arc.

A chess piece can also turn against the one who wields it.

In the distance, Su Qingyao still lay in a pool of blood, her chest's faint rise and fall proving she still breathed.

Chen Ji walked over, bending down to lift her into his arms.

Her body was very light—light enough to break his heart.

"Qingyao," he murmured softly, his voice hoarse beyond recognition, "don't worry, I won't let you forget me."

He raised his head, his gaze fixed on the blurred horizon ahead.

Heavenly Fate's End.

Whatever lay behind that gate, he would find it.

For the third path.

And for her.
